title: Forward contracts establish baseline for arbitrage-free option pricing
claim: Forward prices derived from spot, rate, time to expiration serve as foundation for option valuation
support: Forward price theorem eliminates arbitrage between spot, bonds, and forward contracts
mechanism: Arbitrage-free pricing: two portfolios with identical payoff must have equal value

title: Put-call parity constrains option values
claim: C + PV(K) = P + S; deviations signal arbitrage
support: Synthetic option positions must satisfy parity
mechanism: Risk-neutral replication

title: Historical volatility from log-returns
claim: Standard deviation of log-returns yields historical vol; lookback window tradeoff
support: Log-normal price model justifies log-return measure
mechanism: Vol measures price spread; log-returns approximate additive

title: Implied volatility surface exhibits term structure and skew
claim: Implied vol varies by time-to-expiration and strike; surface is dynamic
support: Market prices embed forward volatility expectations
mechanism: Vol surface captures market beliefs about future realized vol and tail behavior

title: Delta measures option price sensitivity to spot changes
claim: Delta = dPrice/dSpot; ranges 0-1 for calls, -1-0 for puts
support: Enables delta-neutral hedging via dynamic stock holdings
mechanism: Local linear approximation of option price

title: Gamma measures rate of delta change
claim: Gamma = dDelta/dSpot; higher gamma near-ATM requires more frequent rehedging
support: Delta-hedged position P&L = 0.5*Gamma*(dSpot)^2 - Theta*dt
mechanism: Rehedging loss from buying high and selling low as spot moves

title: Theta decay accelerates near expiration
claim: Theta = -dPrice/dt increases in magnitude near expiration
support: Time value approaches zero at expiration; decay accelerates
mechanism: Extrinsic value = time value; as time shrinks, value decays faster

title: Vega captures exposure to implied volatility changes
claim: Vega = dPrice/d(ImpliedVol); positive for long, negative for short
support: Option price increases when implied vol increases
mechanism: Vol enters pricing formula; higher vol = higher option premium

title: Volatility clustering violates constant-vol assumption
claim: Realized vol exhibits positive autocorrelation; high vol today predicts high vol tomorrow
support: Autocorrelation in squared returns is strong and consistent
mechanism: Vol mean-reverts within regimes; vol clusters indicate regime stability

title: Implied vol term structure predicts realized vol direction
claim: Steep term structure signals market expects increasing realized vol
support: Term structure reflects forward expectations
mechanism: Market prices forward vol into long-dated options

title: American options permit early exercise
claim: American call/put exercises early when intrinsic exceeds continuation value
support: Rational exerciser compares immediate payoff vs expected future value
mechanism: Optimal exercise boundary exists and depends on rates, dividends, vol, time

title: Dividends increase early call exercise probability
claim: Ex-dividend date triggers American call exercise spike
support: Dividend reduces stock price; call intrinsic decreases
mechanism: Ex-dividend drop creates exercise incentive to capture dividend

title: Bid-ask spreads widen during vol spikes
claim: Liquidity dries up during vol spikes; spreads widen significantly
support: Market-makers widen spreads during high-vol periods
mechanism: Market-maker inventory risk increases with vol; wider spreads compensate

title: Transaction costs erode small-edge strategies
claim: Strategy edge must exceed 2x round-trip costs to be profitable
support: Empirical observation: most strategies fail due to costs
mechanism: Each round-trip incurs cost; small edge disappears quickly

title: Implied vol skew reflects market-priced jump risk
claim: Puts trade at higher vol than calls (skew); skew widens in crises
support: Skew reflects market concern about downside gaps
mechanism: Options with downside strike have higher vol premium

title: Jump risk creates fat tails exceeding lognormal
claim: Real markets exhibit gaps not captured by lognormal model
support: Return distributions have heavier tails than lognormal
mechanism: Jump-diffusion process better models real returns than pure diffusion

title: Margin creates leverage limits and forced liquidation risk
claim: Broker margin calls force liquidation at unfavorable prices
support: Margin is collateral requirement; leverage amplifies losses
mechanism: Large adverse move forces liquidation; realized loss crystallized

title: Calendar spreads exploit time decay differential
claim: Sell near-term, buy long-term; profit from near-term decay
support: Theta decay accelerates near expiration; near-term decays faster
mechanism: Near-term option loses value faster than long-term premium

title: Long straddle profits when realized vol exceeds implied vol
claim: Buy ATM call+put; profit if realized_vol > implied_vol at entry
support: Straddle gamma drives profit from large moves
mechanism: Gamma P&L = 0.5*gamma*(dSpot)^2 minus theta; net profit if moves > decay

title: Vol forecasting requires regime classification
claim: Realized vol mean-reverts within regimes but jumps between regimes
support: Volatility clustering implies regime stability; regime changes are discontinuous
mechanism: Within-regime mean-reversion breaks at regime boundaries

title: Backtester assumes mid-price; real execution has slippage
claim: Backtest P&L typically overstates real P&L by 30-50% due to slippage
support: Slippage is real; market-makers do not execute at fair value
mechanism: Bid-ask spread is cost of immediacy

title: Dividend dates create discontinuities and assignment risk
claim: Ex-dividend causes stock drop; American call more likely to exercise
support: Corporate dividends are paid; stock drops by dividend amount on ex-date
mechanism: Rational exerciser captures dividend by exercising before ex-date
